newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks push higher at opening.
newsitem.headline: French stocks push higher at opening.

text.p: French shares continued climbing at the start of trading on Friday, building on Thursday's rise of more than one percent.
Traders said the Dow's push past 7,000 overnight, benign bond markets and a strong dollar were all fuelling the CAC's ascent to fresh record highs.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.57 points or 0.29 percent at 2,635.98 at 0917 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 11.5 at 2,646 from Thursday's close.

Lagardere rises 2.13 percent to 168 francs, helped by 1996 sales figures which were in line with expectations, said one broker, whose analyst reiterated the buy rating and saw a target price of 180 francs.
Renault sheds three percent to 126.1 francs, after issuing a fresh warning on 1996 results. It said it expected an operating loss bigger than market estimates.
Havas continues strengthening, up 2.64 percent at 479, buoyed since its capital restructuring with Cie Generale des Eaux.
PSA Peugeot Citroen falls 2.12 percent to 599, slipstreaming Renault.
Gan drops 6.37 percent to 123.5, after its statement that recent rises in the share price were unjustified by fundamentals and it is in talks with the government on its financial problems.
Eurotunnel eases 1.38 percent to 7.15 after reporting 1996 sales at 3.99 billion francs and fourth quarter sales of 1.06 billion.
